mainTopic: How far a husband's written waiver of his wife's property reaches: produce, produce of the produce, and inheritance.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a distinction between one who objects right away (עורר) and one who waits (עומד). אמימר rules that the land itself is acquired, and when רב אשי asks which case he means, אמימר says he does not accept the distinction at all. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a husband who writes 'I have no דין ודברים in your property'. It asks why this is not read as giving up everything, or only the produce, or only the ירושה. אביי answers with יד בעל השטר על התחתונה, בוצינא טב מקרא, and the idea that people give up only uncommon things. רב אשי reads the same result from the word בנכסייך. Next, a ברייתא defines פירות and פירי פירות for רבי יהודה's view. The גמרא then asks which words, 'פירי פירות' or 'עד עולם' or both, are needed. A further question asks whether giving up only the פירי פירות also gives up the first produce; an 'obvious' proof is offered and then knocked down. Finally, רב rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the husband inherits, but not for his reason, and the גמרא begins explaining what he means, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Objecting right away versus waiting
steps.stepSummary: The previous statement applies only to someone who objects right away. If he waits, the other person has acquired the land itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling is about one who objects right away. But if he waits, the other person acquired the land itself from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation from the previous section. It splits the case into two: one who objects at once (עורר) and one who waits (עומד).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the writer protests as soon as the other person comes to take the land, the earlier lenient ruling applies. If he stays quiet and lets the other person take it, he cannot back out, and the land itself belongs to the other person. This two-case split is what רב אשי will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: One who objects or protests right away
One who waits and stays quiet before protesting
The land itself (as opposed to its produce)
They acquired it from him (his act of transfer took effect)

phrases.english: [This is] in the case of one who objects right away.
But in the case of one who waits,
they acquired the land itself from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the distinction drawn just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he objects right away, the earlier ruling applies. If he waits, the land itself is acquired.

steps.title: אמימר rules that the land itself is acquired
steps.stepSummary: אמימר states the practical הלכה: the land itself was acquired from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The הלכה is that they acquired the land itself from him.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a final practical ruling: the written statement transfers the land itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר says nothing about objecting right away or waiting. That leaves open whether his ruling covers both cases or only the case of one who waits. This gap is what sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law is

phrases.english: Ameimar said:

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכְתָא, מִגּוּפָהּ שֶׁל קַרְקַע קָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ.
phrases.english: The law is: they acquired the land itself from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the topic just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land itself is acquired by the written statement.

steps.title: רב אשי asks which case אמימר means
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר whether his ruling is about one who objects right away or one who waits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: Is your ruling about one who objects right away, or one who waits?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks אמימר to make his ruling more precise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 split the case into two. רב אשי wants to know whether אמימר's ruling follows that split, and if so, which side he is ruling on.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
In the case of one who objects, or one who waits?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of אמימר's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ruling cover one who objects right away, or one who waits?

steps.title: Why does this question matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask what practical difference רב אשי's question makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: For which view does this make a practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in with its own side question: according to which view does רב אשי's question matter? This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every view splits the case into 'objects' and 'waits'. So the גמרא checks for whom רב אשי's question actually changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what does it make a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's own side question about רב אשי's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to which opinion does the objects-or-waits question matter?

steps.title: It matters according to רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The difference matters according to the explanation of רב יוסף's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters according to רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own side question. רב אשי's question only matters according to רב יוסף's view, as it was explained in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to that explanation of רב יוסף, the outcome changes depending on whether he objects or waits. A view that does not draw this line would rule the same way in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: According to what רב יוסף said

phrases.english: According to [the view of] Rav Yosef.
phrases.notes: This points back to the split between objecting and waiting explained in step 1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question matters only according to the explanation of רב יוסף.

steps.title: אמימר rejects the distinction
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says 'I did not hear it.' The גמרא explains that he means 'I do not hold of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I have not heard of this. That is to say: I do not agree with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי that he does not accept the split between objecting and waiting. So his ruling applies in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, 'I did not hear it' sounds like he never learned this view. The גמרא explains that it really means 'I do not hold of it.' For אמימר, the land itself is acquired in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it
That is to say
I do not hold of it / I do not agree with it

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא שמיע לי' here does not mean אמימר simply never heard of the view. The גמרא tells us it means he rejects it.
steps.whatToRemember: אמימר: the land itself is acquired in every case. He does not split the case into objecting right away or waiting.

phrases.english: He said to him: I have not heard [this].
That is to say: I do not hold this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמימר rejects the distinction, so his ruling applies in both cases.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: why did he write it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's question: if the husband keeps the produce and his right to inherit, why did he write the waiver?
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] If so, why did he write for her [I have no דין ודברים in your property], etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up a discussion of how far the husband's waiver reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that the husband still eats the produce and inherits from his wife, even though he wrote 'דין ודברים אין לי'. It then asked what the waiver does, and answered that if she sells the land, the sale stands. The גמרא is about to question this narrow reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Etcetera (the quote continues in the source)
Legal claim or involvement (the wording of the husband's waiver)

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן לָמָּה כָּתַב לָהּ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If so, why did he write for her, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The husband had written: 'I have no דין ודברים in your property.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiver only means that if she sells the land, the sale stands. He keeps the produce and his right to inherit.

steps.title: Why not say he gave up everything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wife cannot argue that he removed himself from all rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her say to him: You removed yourself from everything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's narrow reading of the waiver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband wrote a general statement, 'I have no claim in your property.' That sounds like he gave up every right: the produce, the inheritance, and the land. So why does the משנה limit it to her right to sell?

keyTerms.meaning: And let her say to him
From everything
You removed yourself (gave up your rights)

phrases.english: But let her say to him:
You removed yourself from everything!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵימָא לֵיהּ: מִכׇּל מִילֵּי סַלֵּיקְתְּ נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's narrow reading of the husband's waiver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general waiver should cover all of the husband's rights, not just one.

steps.title: A document is read in the narrowest way
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the holder of a document is at a disadvantage, so the waiver is read in the most limited way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The one holding the document has the lower hand.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge with a general rule for reading documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a document's wording is unclear, we read it in the way that gives the least to the person relying on it. Here the wife holds the document, so the husband is treated as giving up only a small part of his rights, not everything.

keyTerms.meaning: The holder of a document is at a disadvantage (unclear wording is read narrowly)

steps.whyThisMatters: יד בעל השטר על התחתונה is a key rule for reading documents, and it comes up often in monetary law.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The hand of the document's holder is on the bottom.
phrases.notes: In other words, the person holding the document gets the weaker reading. Here that is the wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: יַד בַּעַל הַשְּׁטָר עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule for reading documents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general wording means he gave up all his rights.
steps.terutzMaskana: Unclear wording is read in the most limited way, so he gave up only part of his rights.

steps.title: Why not say he gave up only the produce?
steps.stepSummary: If the waiver is read narrowly, why not limit it to the produce, which is worth less than the land?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say [he gave up his rights only] from the produce!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes אביי's own rule further and challenges the משנה again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we must give the wife the smallest possible reading, the produce looks smaller than the right to sell the land itself. So the waiver should cover only the produce, and he should not be able to stop a sale of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (suggests a different reading)
Produce (the income or yield of the property)

phrases.english: But say [he withdrew only] from the produce?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 9 to challenge which right was given up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's view that the waiver covers her right to sell, not the produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The narrowest reading should be the produce, which seems smaller than the right to sell the land.

steps.title: A cucumber now beats a gourd later
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a proverb: what you have now is worth more than something bigger later. The husband values the produce more.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'A cucumber [now] is better than a gourd [later].'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why giving up the produce is not the 'smaller' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband eats the produce right now, so to him it is the more valuable right. The right to block a sale of the land matters to him less in practice. So the narrowest reading is that he gave up only the right to stop her from selling, which is what the משנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Cucumber (a small thing you have now)
Gourd (a bigger thing you would get later)
Better

steps.whatToRemember: The husband's waiver gives up only his right to stop her from selling the land. He keeps the produce, because he values what he has now (בוצינא טב מקרא), and documents are read narrowly (יד בעל השטר על התחתונה).

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"A cucumber is better than a gourd."
phrases.notes: A popular saying: a small thing in your hand now beats a bigger thing you would only get later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A common-sense view of what the husband values
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The produce is the smaller right, so that is what he gave up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce he enjoys now matters more to him, so he gave up only the right to stop a sale of the land.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The waiver lets the wife sell the land, but the husband keeps the produce and his right to inherit.

steps.title: Why not say he gave up his inheritance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the waiver should not be read as giving up the husband's right of ירושה, which seems to be his least valuable right.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say he removed himself from the inheritance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again on אביי's rule that the waiver is read in the most limited way. If we want the smallest right, why not say he only gave up inheriting her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the גמרא explained that the husband values the produce more than the land. Now it points to another candidate: ירושה. That right only matters if she dies first, and he might die before her, so it seems to be worth the least.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us say (introduces another possible reading)
Inheritance: the husband's right to inherit his wife's property

phrases.english: But let us say [he removed himself] from the inheritance!
phrases.notes: Inheritance only helps him if she dies first, so it could be the weakest right he has.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues applying אביי's 'most limited reading' rule to a new candidate right.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the waiver removes only the right to sell the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the waiver is read as narrowly as possible, ירושה seems even weaker than the land itself, so the waiver should apply to it.

steps.title: Death is common, a sale is not
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that death is a common event and selling family land is not. A person only gives up rights in an uncommon matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Death is common; a sale is not common. When a person removes himself, he removes himself from an uncommon matter. From a common matter, a person does not remove himself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the waiver does not cancel the ירושה. People do not give up rights to things that are likely to happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death will certainly happen, so the right of ירושה is real and likely to matter. Selling her inherited land is rare, so giving up rights in a מכירה costs the husband little. The waiver is therefore assumed to cover only the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Common, something that often happens
A sale
Removes himself, gives up his claim

phrases.english: Abaye said: Death is common,
a sale is not common.
And when a person removes himself,
[it is] from a matter that is not common;
from a matter that is common
a person does not remove himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִיתָה שְׁכִיחָא, מְכִירָה לָא שְׁכִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical distinction based on how people usually behave (common versus uncommon events)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ירושה looks like the weakest right, so the waiver should remove it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because death is common, ירושה is a real right he would not give up. The waiver covers only the rare event of a sale.

steps.title: רב אשי reads it from the wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer based on the word בנכסייך ('in your property'). It means the property itself, not its produce, and only during her lifetime, not after her death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'In your property' means not in its produce. 'In your property' means not after death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second, separate way to explain why the waiver removes only the sale. He bases it on the exact word the husband wrote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband wrote that he has no claim 'in your property.' Property is different from the produce it yields, so פירות are not included. Property is also 'yours' only while she is alive, so ירושה after death is not included. All that remains is the right to sell the land during her life.

keyTerms.meaning: In your property: the word written in the waiver
Their produce
After death

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why the waiver removes only the right to sell. אביי says people give up only uncommon things. רב אשי says the word בנכסייך itself excludes produce and inheritance.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'In your property,' and not in their produce;
'In your property,' and not after death.
phrases.notes: After she dies it is no longer 'your' property, so the waiver doesn't reach the inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, בִּנְכָסַיִיךְ וְלֹא בְּפֵירוֹתֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the questions of Steps 10 and 12, in place of אביי's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the document's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We need reasoning about value or how common events are to decide which right was given up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word בנכסייך by itself limits the waiver to the land during her lifetime.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: he always eats the produce of the produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view from the משנה: the husband still eats פירי פירות (produce of the produce).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He always eats the produce of the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה. This quote sets up a discussion of what רבי יהודה meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה said that once the husband waived her property and its produce, he does not eat the produce. רבי יהודה adds that the waiver does not stop him from eating פירי פירות unless he wrote that specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the produce, a second-generation yield
Always

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He always eats the produce of the produce.
phrases.notes: In the משנה he continues: until he writes 'and the produce of their produce forever.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם הוּא אוֹכֵל פֵּירֵי פֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה after finishing the discussion of the waiver.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unless he writes otherwise, the husband's waiver does not stop him from eating פירי פירות.

steps.title: What counts as produce and produce of produce?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how we define פירות and how we define פירי פירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: Which are produce, and which are produce of the produce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that first asks a definition question. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's ruling depends on telling these two kinds of yield apart. So the ברייתא first asks exactly where the line between them falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Which are, what counts as

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Which are produce,
and which are produce of the produce?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן פֵּירוֹת וְאֵלּוּ הֵן פֵּירֵי פֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used by רבי יהודה in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definition of פירות versus פירי פירות

steps.title: Produce from her land versus produce from bought land
steps.stepSummary: Produce grown on the land she brought into the marriage is פירות. If that produce was sold and new land bought with the money, what the new land grows is פירי פירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she brought him land and it produced produce, that is produce. If he sold the produce, bought land with the money, and it produced produce, that is produce of the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with two clear examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First generation: the crops of her original land. Second generation: the crops of land bought with the money from those first crops. That second yield is what רבי יהודה says the husband may still eat.

keyTerms.meaning: She brought in (to the marriage)
Land
He sold... and bought

steps.whatToRemember: פירות = crops from her original land. פירי פירות = crops from land bought with the money of those crops.

phrases.english: If she brought him land and it produced produce,
these are produce.
If he sold the produce and bought land with them,
and it produced produce,
these are produce of the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Crops of her original land are פירות. Crops of land bought with the proceeds of those crops are פירי פירות.

steps.title: Which words does רבי יהודה require?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, for רבי יהודה, the essential words are 'produce of the produce,' or 'forever,' or both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked of them: According to רבי יהודה, is 'produce of the produce' specifically required, or perhaps 'forever' specifically, or perhaps both specifically?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question about what exactly the husband must write to block even the פירי פירות. It lists three possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's full phrase is 'the produce of their produce forever.' The question is which part does the work. Is one phrase enough by itself, or must both appear?

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them, a genuine open question
Specifically, exactly this and nothing less
Forever
Both of them

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
According to Rabbi Yehuda, is 'produce of the produce' specifically [required],
or perhaps 'forever' specifically,
or perhaps both of them specifically?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה פֵּירֵי פֵירוֹת דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יהודה's ruling and asks which part of the required wording is essential.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'פירי פירות', 'עד עולם', or both are required for the waiver to cover the second-generation produce

steps.title: If 'produce of produce' is enough, why say 'forever'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the first option: if 'produce of the produce' alone works, why does the משנה also include 'forever'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'produce of the produce' is specifically what is needed, why do I need 'forever'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins working through the three options. It challenges the first one, since 'forever' would seem to be an extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one phrase is enough, the second phrase in רבי יהודה's wording looks unnecessary. A משנה is not expected to include useless words, so this option needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, if you conclude
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: If you say
'produce of the produce' specifically,
why do I need 'forever'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר פֵּירֵי פֵירוֹת דַּוְקָא, עַד עוֹלָם לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the first option raised in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that 'פירי פירות' alone is sufficient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, the word 'עד עולם' in רבי יהודה's wording would be extra.

steps.title: 'Produce of produce' already means 'forever'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'forever' teaches us something: writing 'produce of the produce' already counts as if he had written 'forever.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: since he wrote to her 'produce of the produce,' it is as if he wrote to her 'forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the first option. The word 'forever' is not extra; it explains what 'produce of the produce' already means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who gives up even the produce of the produce has shown that he is giving up all future yields endlessly. So 'forever' is just spelling out what that phrase already includes, and the phrase alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
It is like one who wrote...

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer to the open question. The גמרא is only showing how the first option could hold up against the 'extra word' challenge.

phrases.english: This teaches us:
since he wrote to her 'produce of the produce,'
it is like one who wrote to her 'forever.'

steps.title: If 'forever' is the key word, why mention 'produce of the produce'?

steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the challenge in step 19, only reversed. If 'עד עולם' alone works, the phrase 'פירי פירות' seems like extra wording that adds nothing.

steps.title: 'Produce of the produce' teaches that without 'forever' it does not work
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'פירי פירות' is there to teach that even after writing it, only adding 'עד עולם' makes it work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: even though he wrote 'produce of the produce,' if he also wrote 'forever,' yes, it works; if not, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'פירי פירות' is mentioned to teach a lesson: writing it alone is not enough.

steps.title: If both phrases are needed, why two phrases?

steps.title: Why 'forever' is needed besides 'produce of the produce'
steps.stepSummary: Without 'עד עולם', we would think he gave up only the second round of produce but can still eat the third round.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed: if he wrote 'produce of the produce' but not 'forever,' I would think it is only the produce of the produce that he does not eat, but the produce of the produce of the produce he does eat. That is why 'forever' is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with צריכא: both phrases are needed. This step explains the first half, why 'עד עולם' is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פירי פירות' alone covers only one round, the second generation of produce. 'עד עולם' stretches the giving-up to every later round, with no end.

steps.simpleTranslation: And if he wrote 'forever' but not 'produce of the produce,' I would think 'forever' goes on the produce. That is why 'produce of the produce' is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the צריכא answer by explaining why 'פירי פירות' is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עד עולם' by itself would attach to the plain produce, meaning he gives up the produce forever but keeps the produce of the produce. Writing 'פירי פירות' points 'עד עולם' at the later rounds too.

keyTerms.meaning: stands on, refers to
on the produce
for this reason

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, he must write both: 'פירי פירות' shows he means the later produce, and 'עד עולם' makes it reach every round forever.

phrases.english: And if he wrote to her 'forever'

I would have thought:

steps.title: If he gave up only the produce of the produce, may he eat the produce?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: the husband wrote that he has no claim to her property or to the פירי פירות. Can he still eat the first produce?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he wrote to her, 'I have no claim to your property or to the produce of the produce,' may he eat the produce? Did he give up only the produce of the produce but not the produce, or did he give up everything?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The husband skipped the plain produce in his document, so does he keep his right to it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see it. Either he gave up only what he named, the second round, and keeps the first produce, or naming the second round automatically means giving up everything before it.

keyTerms.meaning: they asked (an open question raised in the בית מדרש)
a legal claim

steps.title: Obviously he gave up everything, since produce of the produce comes from the produce
steps.stepSummary: It is obvious he gave up everything: if he ate the first produce, there would be no פירי פירות left to give up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that he gave up everything. Because if you say he gave up only the produce of the produce and not the produce, once he eats the produce, where would produce of the produce come from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the question is easy: he gave up everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 17 we know the produce of the produce is grown on land bought with the first produce. If the husband ate the first produce, nothing would be left to buy new land, so his giving up the produce of the produce would mean nothing. That is why it must include the first produce.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He gave up everything, because the produce of the produce cannot exist if he eats the first produce.

steps.title: The same question would hit רבי יהודה in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'obvious' answer of Step 27. רבי יהודה in the משנה also speaks of a husband who eats the first produce but not the פירי פירות. So there must be a case where some produce was left over, and our case can be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your logic, what about the משנה where רבי יהודה says he always eats the פירי פירות? If he eats the first produce, where would פירי פירות come from? You must say it is where some produce was left over. Here too, it is where he left some over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof that the husband must have given up the first produce too. It shows that this proof would also make the words of the משנה impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 argued that if the first produce is eaten, nothing would be left to become פירי פירות. But the same problem applies to רבי יהודה's words in the משנה: there too the first produce gets eaten, yet he speaks of פירי פירות. So the answer must be that some produce was left over, perhaps used to buy land. Our case can work the same way, so the proof falls away and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, meaning your logic would cause a problem elsewhere too
Produce of the produce, the second round of profit
Where he left some over

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא now proves he may eat the first produce. It only knocks down the proof that he may not, so the question is left without a firm answer.

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,

phrases.english: He always eats the produce of the produce, etc.
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה. He keeps eating the פירי פירות unless he writes those off too.

phrases.english: Since he eats the produce,

Rather, it is a case where some was left over,

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same logic would make רבי יהודה's words in the משנה impossible. Leftover produce makes פירי פירות possible even when he eats the first produce.

steps.title: רב rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but not for his reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. רב rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but not because of his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, etc. רב said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but not for his reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view in the משנה. רב gives a ruling that agrees with his result but not with his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the husband still inherits his wife even if he wrote that he gives up all claims. His reason is that the condition goes against the Torah. רב accepts that the husband inherits, but says the reason is different. This opens a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה follows the opinion of
But not for his reason

steps.title: What does 'not for his reason' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב means when he says the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but not for his reason.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of רב's unusual ruling. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will try to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agreeing with a ruling while rejecting its reason is unclear. Which part does רב accept, and what reason does he use instead? The גמרא needs to define this before it can move on.

keyTerms.meaning: What

phrases.english: What does 'the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel'

steps.title: First explanation: the husband's inheritance is rabbinic and strengthened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב agrees the husband inherits her. Unlike רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רב holds that a condition against the Torah normally works. Here it fails because a husband's inheritance is דרבנן, and the חכמים made their rules stronger than Torah rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said that if she dies he inherits her, but not for his reason. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a condition against the Torah is void, while רב holds such a condition stands. But רב holds that a husband's inheritance is דרבנן, and the חכמים made their words stronger than Torah words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first way to understand רב. He agrees with the result that the husband inherits, but he gets there through a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the condition fails because it goes against the Torah. רב holds that such a condition normally does work. So why does the husband still inherit? Because a husband's inheritance is only דרבנן, and the חכמים protected their own rules even more strongly, so they cannot be cancelled by a condition. The אילימא ('if you say') wording shows this is only a first suggestion, which the גמרא may still test.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, the opening of a suggested explanation
One who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah
His condition is void / his condition stands
A husband's inheritance of his wife is a rabbinic law
Reinforcement, extra strength

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that a rabbinic rule is harder to cancel than a Torah rule. That is exactly the point: the חכמים gave their own rules extra protection.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains how רב can reach the same הלכה as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל while holding the opposite view on conditions against the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: If you say: the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who said: if she dies, he inherits her,
but not for his reason,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר:
phrases.english: for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
one who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void,
while Rav holds: his condition stands,
but he holds: a husband's inheritance is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: This is רב's own reason. The inheritance itself comes from the חכמים, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: and the Sages gave reinforcement to their words
more than to those of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first suggested answer to the question of Step 30
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first suggestion (אילימא): רב accepts that the husband inherits. He holds that conditions against the Torah normally work, but a husband's inheritance is דרבנן and was strengthened by the חכמים, so it cannot be cancelled. The אילימא wording marks this as a proposal, not a settled answer.
